newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech bank 96 net profit CZK 1.85 bln.
newsitem.headline: Czech bank 96 net profit CZK 1.85 bln.

text.p: Ceska Sporitelna a.s., the largest Czech savings bank, on Monday said it posted a 1996 net profit of 1.85 billion crowns, according to unaudited preliminary figures, up from 263 million in 1995.
The bank added that the results, which were calculated according to Czech accounting standards, were submitted to the Prague Stock Exchange last week.
Kamil Ziegler, a senior bank official, would not comment on and possible dividends for 1996.
He added that results calculated according to international accounting standards had been calculated, but were not available for release.
The PSE show the bank's total assets at the end of 1996 were 359.7 billion crowns, down from 367.85 billion at the end of the previous year.
Sporitelna's 1995 gross profit was 9.17 billion crowns but the bank assigned 9.13 billion to its reserves covering "classified" loans where recovery is seen as doubtful at best.
Ziegler did not elaborate on the results.
Sporitelna shares on the Prague Stock Exchange closed down nine crowns on Monday at 318, though the 1996 results were released after the bourse closed.
